rules.source: Personal Data Processing Law (Fizisko personu datu apstrādes likums) alongside Regulation (EU) 2016/679 — Data State Inspectorate https://www.dvi.gov.lv/en/departments and https://linklaters.com/insights/data-protected/data-protected---latvia
rules.retrieved_snippet: DVI page (fetched): the Inspectorate "also serves as a supervisory authority for personal data processing, as defined by the General Data Protection Regulation" and its status as a state administrative body is based on the Latvian personal data processing law; Linklaters: the GDPR and the Personal Data Processing Law are the primary legal acts and a separate law covers processing in criminal and administrative offence proceedings.

rules.source: Criminal Law Section 241 (arbitrary access to automated data processing systems) — Council of Europe Octopus Latvia page — https://www.coe.int/en/web/octopus/-/latvia
rules.retrieved_snippet: Council of Europe Octopus profile lists section 241 (arbitrary access) with related offences in sections 243 and 245; Latvia signed the Budapest Convention on 05.05.2004 and ratified it on 14.04.2007. Current text and penalties of section 241 not retrieved.

rules.source: Consumer Rights Protection Law (Patērētāju tiesību aizsardzības likums) — Consumer Rights Protection Centre https://ptac.gov.lv/en/about-us
rules.retrieved_snippet: The Centre operates under the Consumer Rights Protection Law, which implements Directives 2011/83, 93/13 and 1999/44; it investigates complaints, adopts decisions binding on traders and offers conciliation; the Saeima approved amendments on 14 September 2023 introducing consumer class actions under Directive 2020/1828 (entry into force not confirmed). Current consolidated text not verified.

rules.source: Criminal Law Section 78 (incitement to national, ethnic and racial hatred) — Council of Europe ECRI government comments https://rm.coe.int/government-comments-on-the-5th-report-on-latvia/1680934aa0
rules.retrieved_snippet: Government comments to ECRI describe Section 78 as criminalising acts directed towards inciting national, ethnic or racial hatred, with liability dependent on subjective attitude; secondary reports give a base penalty of up to three years' imprisonment, community service or a fine and up to 10 years for aggravated forms. Wording changed over time; current consolidated text not retrieved.

rules.source: Protection of the Rights of the Child Law (consolidated as of 6 March 2014) and Electronic Mass Media Law Article 232 — https://better-internet-for-kids.europa.eu/en/knowledge-hub/rules-guidelines/protection-rights-child-law-consolidated-amendments-6-march-2014
rules.retrieved_snippet: Better Internet for Kids lists the child-rights law (first enacted 1998) which defines abuse broadly (emotional cruelty, sexual abuse, neglect and other treatment endangering a child's health, life, development or self-respect); a Council of Europe mapping cites Article 232 of the Electronic Mass Media Law requiring video-sharing platforms to act against content that may harm minors. Machine-translated 2014 consolidation; current text not verified.
